decisions.reason: A complete same-message MODIFY already requires the NFT referral-count attribute to reflect the NFT's current credited referral count, so no duplicate or edit is needed.
The candidate already requires public referral statistics to reflect recorded activity, and the source reports those leaderboard and page-summary counts as correct; only the NFT attributes are stale.
The source confirms ticket accounting as correct and changes only referral-count accuracy in NFT attributes.
The source exposes an earnings-display failure but does not revise the candidate's existing commission-accounting rules; the same-message runtime failure already records the observed mismatch.
Referral-count accuracy in NFT attributes does not change the dashboard NFT-ownership inventory rule.
The source concerns numeric NFT attributes, not image, cover, or wallet-media rendering.
The source does not change how completed mints are counted in public platform statistics.
The referral-count attribute rule has no necessary effect on the public sales-remaining countdown.
The source does not establish or change any prize-pool statistic behavior.
NFT referral-count visibility does not affect success-modal timing, token IDs, or finalization controls.
The source identifies a live NFT-attribute accuracy rule but does not request any FAQ or explanatory-copy change.
Displaying an NFT's current credited referral count does not change which referral codes are valid or whether self-referral is allowed.
